blogPosts.title: How Much Does a Warehouse Development Cost in Southbank in 2026?
blogPosts.excerpt: Breaking down the costs of building a warehouse in Southbank, including land, materials, labour, and council fees for Melbourne industrial projects.
body: If you're looking at developing a warehouse in Southbank or anywhere across inner Melbourne, the big question is always cost. In 2026, warehouse development costs vary depending on size, height, site conditions, and whether you need specialised fitouts like cool rooms or high-bay racking. For a standard 1,000-square-metre warehouse in Southbank, you're looking at anywhere from $1.2 million to $1.8 million for a basic shell, plus fitout costs. That includes slab, steel frame, cladding, roofing, and basic electrical and plumbing.

Site preparation can add significant cost, especially in Southbank where some industrial sites sit on reclaimed land or require deep foundations. You might need geotechnical surveys, groundwater management, and environmental remediation if the site had previous industrial use. Budget between $50,000 and $150,000 for site prep on a mid-sized block. Then there's council approvals, which in Melbourne's inner suburbs can take 6 to 12 months and cost anywhere from $10,000 to $40,000 depending on the complexity.

Materials costs have stabilised after the post-COVID spike, but steel and concrete remain high due to ongoing demand for infrastructure projects across Victoria. In 2026, expect to pay around $1,200 per tonne for structural steel and $250 per cubic metre for ready-mix concrete. Labour costs in Melbourne are also up, with skilled trades in short supply. You'll pay premium rates for steel erectors, concreters, and electricians — factor in $80 to $120 per hour for most commercial trades.

One way to control costs is to go with a design and construct contractor like Cota Group. We handle the entire process from concept to handover, which eliminates the costly back-and-forth between separate architects, engineers, and builders. Our fixed-price contracts in Southbank mean you know exactly what you're paying from day one. No variations unless you change the scope. We also have established relationships with suppliers across Melbourne, so we pass on material discounts directly to you.

Don't forget ongoing costs like fire services, compliance with the Building Code of Australia, and energy efficiency requirements. A modern warehouse in Southbank needs fire sprinklers, emergency lighting, and sometimes a fire hydrant booster. Sustainability features like solar panels and LED lighting can save you money long-term but add upfront cost. Many clients recoup their solar investment within 3 to 5 years, especially with current electricity prices.

Finally, think about access and amenities. Does your warehouse need dock levellers, drive-in doors, or a mezzanine office? Each feature adds cost but improves functionality. A basic 500-square-metre warehouse in Southbank with a small office might cost $1,800 per square metre, while a high-spec distribution centre with climate control and automation could hit $3,000 per square metre. Get in touch with Cota Group for a site-specific quote — we'll walk you through every line item.

blogPosts.title: Design and Construct vs Traditional Build: What's Best for Melbourne Commercial Projects?
blogPosts.excerpt: Comparing design and construct with traditional building methods for commercial and industrial projects in Southbank and Melbourne.
body: For commercial and industrial projects in Southbank and across Melbourne, the choice between design and construct and traditional building is critical. Design and construct means one contractor handles both design and construction, giving you a single point of accountability. Traditional build separates the architect from the builder, which can lead to coordination headaches and cost blowouts. For most Melbourne businesses, D&C wins hands-down for speed and cost certainty.

With design and construct, the contractor controls the full chain. At Cota Group, we have in-house designers, engineers, and project managers. That means we can start site preparation while finalising design details, cutting weeks off the timeline. On a typical Southbank warehouse, a D&C approach can shave 3 to 4 months off the traditional schedule. That's earlier revenue for your business and less time paying holding costs on the land.

Traditional building contracts in Melbourne often end up with variations. The architect designs something, the builder prices it, and the client finds out it's over budget. Then you go back and redesign. It's slow and frustrating. With D&C, we design to your budget from the start. If you have a $2 million cap for a Southbank industrial fitout, we design a building that hits that number. No surprises, no redesigns, no wasted fees.

Quality doesn't suffer with D&C. In fact, because the same team is responsible for design and construction, there's built-in accountability. If a detail doesn't work on site, we fix it immediately. Cota Group follows rigorous quality management processes — regular inspections, material testing, and sign-offs at every stage. Our Southbank projects consistently pass building inspections first time because we build it right from the start.

Another advantage is communication. In a traditional build, the client has to manage the architect, engineer, builder, and subcontractors separately. With D&C, you talk to one project manager. We handle the rest. For busy business owners in Southbank and Melbourne, that's invaluable. You get regular updates without being dragged into technical details. We report on budget, timeline, and any risks early.

There are cases where a traditional approach might still be suitable — if you have a heritage building or a highly specific architectural design that requires a separate architect. But for most commercial and industrial projects in Melbourne, D&C is the smarter choice. It's faster, cheaper, and less stressful. At Cota Group, we've delivered over 150 projects using this model. If you're planning a build in Southbank, call us to discuss which approach suits your project best.

blogPosts.title: Commercial Industrial Fitout Costs in Melbourne: A 2026 Guide
blogPosts.excerpt: A detailed breakdown of costs for industrial fitouts in Melbourne, including offices, amenities, and mezzanines for Southbank warehouses.
body: If you're fitting out an industrial space in Southbank or anywhere in Melbourne, costs vary widely based on what you need. A basic warehouse fitout with a small office, restroom, and break room might cost $200,000 to $400,000 for a 500-square-metre space. Add a mezzanine, and you're looking at another $150,000 to $300,000 depending on size and load rating. Every fitout is different, so always get a site-specific quote.

The main cost drivers for industrial fitouts in Melbourne include partitioning, electrical, plumbing, HVAC, and flooring. For a Southbank warehouse, you'll likely need metal stud walls for offices, painted plasterboard finishes, and commercial-grade carpet or vinyl. Electrical costs cover lighting, power points, data cabling, and switchboards. Expect to pay $80 to $150 per square metre for electrical alone in a commercial industrial setting.

Plumbing costs depend on whether you need a kitchenette, bathrooms, or a trade waste system. A simple staff bathroom and break room sink might cost $15,000 to $30,000. Full amenities with showers, multiple toilets, and a kitchen can run $50,000 to $80,000. If your operation involves process water or chemical waste, you'll need a licensed plumber to handle trade waste compliance — budget extra for that.

HVAC is another big ticket item. A split system for a small office in a Southbank warehouse might cost $5,000 to $10,000 installed. But if you need ducted air conditioning for a larger office or a temperature-controlled storage area, costs climb to $50,000 to $150,000. Consider energy-efficient reverse-cycle units to save on power bills. Many clients also add ceiling insulation and high-performance glazing to reduce HVAC load.

Mezzanines are popular in Melbourne industrial fitouts because they effectively double your floor space without expanding your footprint. A steel mezzanine rated for 5 kPa (office use) costs around $400 to $600 per square metre installed. Heavy-duty mezzanines for storage can hit $800 per square metre. Make sure your engineer certifies the load capacity and that the installation complies with the Building Code of Australia.

At Cota Group, we manage industrial fitouts from design to handover, coordinating all trades and ensuring council compliance. Our Southbank projects include everything from basic amenities to high-spec offices with feature joinery. We work with your budget and timeline, and we always provide a fixed-price contract upfront. Contact us at our Southbank office to discuss your fitout needs — we'll give you a realistic cost estimate based on your specific requirements.

blogPosts.title: Six Steps to a Successful Commercial Build in Southbank
blogPosts.excerpt: A practical guide to planning and executing a commercial construction project in Southbank, from concept to handover.
body: Starting a commercial build in Southbank or anywhere across Melbourne can feel overwhelming. But breaking it down into clear steps makes the process manageable. At Cota Group, we guide our clients through every phase — from initial concept to final handover. Here's a practical six-step roadmap to help you plan your next commercial or industrial project in Southbank. Follow this, and you'll avoid most common pitfalls.

Step one is defining your brief. What do you need? A warehouse, an office fitout, or a full industrial complex? Think about size, layout, access, and any special requirements like cool rooms, high ceilings, or loading docks. The clearer your brief, the more accurate your budget and timeline will be. Visit similar buildings in Southbank to get ideas. Write everything down — it becomes the foundation of your design.

Step two is choosing your delivery model. We strongly recommend design and construct for Southbank commercial projects. It saves time, money, and stress. Interview a few D&C contractors and ask for examples of similar projects they've delivered in Melbourne. Check their licences, insurance, and safety records. At Cota Group, we're happy to show you around our completed Southbank developments so you can see the quality first-hand.

Step three is design and approvals. Your contractor's design team will turn your brief into architectural drawings and engineering plans. This stage includes site surveys, geotechnical investigations, and council liaison. In Southbank, council approvals can take 3 to 6 months for commercial projects. Your contractor should manage all submissions and handle any objections. We've navigated City of Melbourne and Port Phillip planning processes many times.

Step four is construction. Once permits are issued, we break ground. Your project manager will schedule trades, order materials, and run site meetings. Expect weekly progress updates and site walkthroughs. Quality and safety checks happen throughout. A 500-square-metre warehouse in Southbank typically takes 6 to 9 months from start to finish. Larger developments can take 12 to 18 months. Your contractor should stick to the agreed timeline.

Step five is commissioning and handover. Before you move in, we test everything — electrical, plumbing, fire services, HVAC. We fix any defects and provide you with operation manuals, warranties, and certificates of compliance. Step six is post-construction support. A good contractor stays in touch. At Cota Group, we offer a 12-month defects liability period and are always available for questions. Ready to start your Southbank build? Call us today.
